newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: ASIAN MTBE-PRODUCERS RAISE OFFERS TO THE $300 MARK.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN MTBE-PRODUCERS RAISE OFFERS TO THE $300 MARK.

text.p: The Asian MTBE market sought direction from Thailand's Bangchak Petroleum Plc buy tender as producers raised their offers to the $300-mark.
"There hasn't been too much change...supplies are still tight and prices should be firmer," said one producer.
Producers in Asia and the Middle East upped their offers to "at least $300" per tonne on a free-on-board Singapore basis for September lots, citing earlier deals done at $295.
"Buyers have to take the price because of U.S. price is so good," reasoned another producer.
They said with U.S. west coast prices around $330 per tonne, there was still a wide margin of profit to be made with freight at around $25.
Malaysia sold a spot cargo of up to 15,000-tonnes in September to a U.S. trader and also is targetting its next spot availability in October to the U.S., sources said.
But some traders were less bullish and said producers were just hiking up prices.
"Already the arbitrage trade has calmed down," a trader said.
The September market should not be supported by the U.S. as the October arrival price was not that attractive, said a trader.
The high offers were also keeping a lid on regional demand, traders said.
Also, supplies are due to ease the tightness as three producers are moving supplies to Asia during the second half of August.

"There should be a peak by the end of August, and then you may not see any more gaps in the arbitrage," said one trader. Sources said Bangchak's tender to buy 1,500 tonnes for delivery in September which closes Wednesday and is valid for a day, will provide clearer direction.
In its last tender nearly a month ago, Bangchak bought a cargo for August delivery at around $275 per tonne on a cost-and-freight basis to Thailand from Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
